real_qa.q: What does peer-reviewed science say about microplastics in the human brain?
real_qa.r: The claim that we have a spoonful of microplastics in our brains is based on a study using a technique proven not to work—other scientists confirmed the method does not function properly. Additionally, it would take 10,000 years to ingest six grams of plastic, making it impossible to have accumulated a thousand times more plastic in your brain than you have ever breathed and eaten in your lifetime.

real_qa.q: What is the actual composition of plastic in ocean gyres versus media claims?
real_qa.r: There is no floating island the size of Texas—that myth was created and debunked through a PhD thesis. What actually exists in the gyres is approximately 85% fishing gear which does cause harm, while consumer items such as bottles, straws, and bags combined represent only 0.03% of the total plastic and are not proven to cause any harm.
real_qa.requete: Great Pacific Garbage Patch size Texas myth

real_qa.q: What does scientific research show about the environmental impact of plastic versus alternative materials?
real_qa.r: Plastic is half a percent of all materials used and grows at the same rate as concrete, metal, glass, and paper. According to life cycle studies, plastics are the greenest, lowest impact choice nine times out of 10. Alternative materials create four times more waste, three times more greenhouse gas, more litter, and cost more. A McKinsey study from 2025 (Noder Gordon et al.) shows consumers incorrectly believe glass jars are the best option when studies prove they have the worst environmental impact.
real_qa.requete: plastic environmental impact life cycle studies versus glass metal

real_qa.q: Why do journalists reporting on microplastics differ dramatically from scientific consensus?
real_qa.r: A scientific study comparing journalist reporting to scientist research found that the vast majority of scientific studies say there is no evidence of harm from microplastics, while 93% of journalist articles claim there is a definite threat. The FDA and scientific consensus after thousands of studies over 50 years agree there is no threat, yet journalists report the opposite daily.

real_qa.q: How do the weight and environmental costs of different straws compare?
real_qa.r: No straw has zero weight and is the greenest option. A plastic straw weighs less than one gram, a paper straw weighs two grams, a metal straw weighs 20 grams, and a glass straw weighs 30 grams. Weight nearly correlates with environmental impact and cost—the more something weighs, the more it costs and the worse it is for the environment.
real_qa.requete: plastic paper metal glass straw weight environmental impact

real_qa.q: What does the EPA lead copper rule indicate about copper pipe toxicity in drinking water?
real_qa.r: Copper is toxic at one part per million in drinking water, and there are proven cases of poisoning from copper pipes—not theoretical but actually occurring. The EPA's lead copper rule requires annual water testing from homes to check for lead and copper because it is so poisonous. Plastic pipes pass safety tests while copper pipes fail if water is not at neutral pH.
real_qa.requete: copper pipes toxicity one part per million EPA lead copper rule
